objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (19 November 2026), challenging A106 (and A107): using the proved identification theorem as the reader, classify starts of 5 to 20 knots under at least two weightings other than SCALE-SHARE's, chosen and frozen before looking, one of them a weighting where stalls do not dominate; report per weighting and size the share in the proved class and the dimension shares in it. Advisor before the freeze on which weightings are honest contrasts. Stop at the table, or at a weighting under which three dimensions or exponential growth becomes common in the class. Serves G17.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Successful, 10 of 11 held, W7 failed; referee pending; Narrowing): two dimensions are typical of the weighting, not of the growth. Read by the proved theorem, uniform random trees (no stall, every start in the class) grow in three or more dimensions in 12% of growers at twelve knots and 37% at twenty, up to six; Poisson(1) extra lines make exponential growth 11-41% of in-class growers; the configuration model and growth by attachment keep two (80-100%, three never). A bare tree of knots of at most five places is a caterpillar with at most two chains (post hoc, proved); a dead hub gives three within five places. 1,226 of 1,226 regrown agree. A106 overturned as a reading of the growth.
